Few careers hold my attention like mechanical engineering, especially the challenge of turning ideas into practical systems that improve everyday life. Ever since I was young, I have been fascinated by how machines work, and that curiosity grew into a clear commitment to building solutions that are efficient, reliable, and made to last. It is for this reason that I am certain of my desire to continue developing as a Mechanical Engineer. I am originally from Nigeria, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500. Across my academic and project work, I have completed 7 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in translating complex mechanical problems into designs that work not only in theory but also in production and use. One example came when I needed to use a new engineering tool for a project; within a few weeks I was using it confidently, and soon afterwards I was helping teammates set up their first models and avoid the early mistakes I had already worked through.

My experience has also shown me how much I value solving difficult technical problems in ways that can be applied beyond a single task. In one project, I developed an original solution to a mechanical design problem that others had not managed to resolve, and the approach was later taken up outside my own team for similar work. On another occasion, colleagues began coming to me with questions in my own area, asking me to review calculations or talk through design choices before they moved ahead. Beyond the technical side, one of my favourite memories was taking my family to a science and engineering exhibition where they saw a prototype I had helped develop and immediately started asking questions about every moving part. Hearing a younger relative proudly tell strangers, “They build things that actually work!” made this career feel especially meaningful. I am now eager to bring my training, practical mindset, and enthusiasm to a Mechanical Engineer role where I can contribute dependable solutions and continue growing through real engineering challenges.

reference_text:
Few things are more satisfying to me than taking raw materials and shaping them into something lasting, useful, and beautifully made. What first drew me to carpentry was that blend of creativity and hands-on problem-solving: the chance to build spaces and furniture that become part of people’s daily lives. One of my favourite memories is bringing my family to see a community project I had helped build, only for a younger relative to run straight to a handcrafted bench and proudly tell everyone, “They made this.” That moment stayed with me because it captured exactly why this work matters to me. I am originally from Spain, and it is for this reason that I am certain of my desire to continue developing as a Carpenter, creating work that is both practical and meaningful.

My academic route has given me a strong foundation for this path. I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100, and across my studies and applied work I completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes. That experience taught me how to approach work methodically and carry ideas through to a finished result. When I needed to use a new digital design and planning tool that was unfamiliar to me, I built confidence with it gradually over more than a year of steady use, until it became part of how I prepared and checked work. In one team setting, repeated delays were being caused by measurements and material adjustments not lining up smoothly on site, so I introduced a simple step-by-step checking sheet that helped us catch issues earlier and keep the job moving.

I also value the practical exchange of knowledge that good work depends on. In my own area, colleagues have sometimes come to me with questions about planning details and fit, and I have enjoyed talking through options with them clearly and directly. Combined with my interest in reading a space carefully, measuring accurately, and producing clean, durable work, these experiences have confirmed the kind of Carpenter I want to be: someone who contributes reliable workmanship, thoughtful solutions, and genuine pride in what is built.

What continues to engage me is the way a library can turn curiosity into confidence, whether someone is beginning a research project, looking for their next novel, or simply searching for a welcoming place to start. My perspective was shaped further through doctoral study at a university ranked in the global top 100, where I completed a Doctorate and saw how access to well-organised knowledge can change the pace and quality of people’s work. That experience taught me to approach questions by looking not only at the information requested, but also at the clearest route to it. Pursuing a Librarian role is therefore a natural continuation of what has long motivated me: a love of stories, learning, and helping people discover resources that feel both useful and inviting.

In one role, I needed to use a new digital tool for organising and retrieving materials; within a few weeks I was using it confidently, and soon afterwards I was showing colleagues how to get started so they could use it in their own work. When a recurring issue in locating and tracking frequently requested items was slowing the team down, I introduced a simple workaround that streamlined the process and reduced repeated delays. Colleagues also sometimes came to me with questions in my own area, and I became someone they would ask when they wanted help untangling a search or identifying the most relevant source. Across my work, I have completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, and I bring that same practical focus to every setting. Originally from Colombia, I am especially drawn to creating welcoming spaces where curiosity can grow for people of all ages. One of my favourite memories is watching a young family member proudly use their very first library card at one of my community events, then asking me to recommend “a book with adventure and dragons.” That moment captured exactly why this work matters to me, and what I hope to contribute as a librarian.
